description:
FILED s473r (2026-09-07) from the #1514 probe set, both PRE-EXISTING (byte-identical on a bfa11c72 extraction) and both the boundless-integer model (#1513, USER-ruled DOCUMENTED).  Two spellings of one fact: PCL keeps an EXACT INTEGER where perl has an NV, and above 2**53 the two stringify differently and round differently.

REPRODUCERS, probed against perl 5.40.3:

 (a) int() of a double past the IV range.
       perl -e "printf qq{%s\n}, int(1e20)"    ->  1e+20
       ./runpcl  same program                  ->  100000000000000000000
     p-int truncates the double to an exact bignum; perl leaves an NV, because
     the value does not fit an IV.  Same for -1e20.

 (b) EXACT integer division past 2**53 answers an integer.
       perl -e "printf qq{%s\n}, 9007199254740992/2"  ->  4.5035996273705e+15
       ./runpcl  same program                          ->  4503599627370496
     PCL answers the exact quotient (perl does this too for small IVs -- 10/5
     is 2 in both) but perl has left IV territory here and prints the NV.

 (c) INEXACT integer division past 2**53 rounds DIFFERENTLY, and perl is the
     one that loses precision first.
       perl -e "printf qq{%.17g\n}, 9007199254740993/7"  ->  1286742750677284.5
       ./runpcl  same program                             ->  1286742750677284.8
     perl converts BOTH operands to NVs and divides those, so 2**53+1 becomes
     2**53 before the division.  %p-divide-general builds the exact rational
     and rounds it once, which is the mathematically correct answer and not
     perl`s.  NOTE the direction: this is a case where PCL is MORE accurate
     than perl, and #1514`s new `(signed-byte 53)` fast arm -- which divides
     two exactly-representable doubles -- is perl`s own algorithm; it declines
     exactly here, which is why the guard row `div-o53` in
     Pl/t/perf-levers-04.t asserts PCL`s answer and names this task.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is not local.  Making (b) and (c) answer
perl would mean coercing every integer division past 2**53 to a double, which
is the 64-bit boundary #1513 rules PCL does NOT implement (pack/unpack and
Math::BigInt depend on exact big integers).  Any fix must come from that
decision, not from p-int or p-/.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: a perl-tests or companion row that fails ONLY because of
one of these three shapes.  None does today -- the full sweep is TOTAL 18674
with the #1514 lever in, and op/int.t is OK 19/0.

=== s473a (2026-09-07, Opus): FOLDED INTO THE #1513 SECTION, as this task asked ===
All three shapes are now in `docs/not-supported.md` Â§"Integers are unbounded:
PCL has no 64-bit boundary" as a second table, naming this task as their owner
and `Pl/t/perf-levers-04.t`'s `div-o53` row as their guard.  Re-verified on the
rebased tree (main 89566d77) against perl 5.40.3, byte for byte:

  printf "%s\n",    int(1e20)                perl 1e+20              PCL 100000000000000000000
  printf "%s\n",    9007199254740992/2       perl 4.5035996273705e+15 PCL 4503599627370496
  printf "%.17g\n", 9007199254740993/7       perl 1286742750677284.5  PCL 1286742750677284.8

The section states the third one's direction explicitly â PCL is the MORE
accurate side, because perl converts both operands to NVs before dividing â
so a future reader does not "fix" it into perl's rounding by accident.  The
task stays OPEN as the pointer #1513's revisit trigger would reopen; nothing
is owed unless a row fails for one of these three reasons.
subject: DIVERGENCE, pre-existing, the #1513 boundless-integer model (USER: DOCUMENTED, not implemented): above 2**53 PCL keeps an EXACT integer where perl has an NV -- `int(1e20)` prints 100000000000000000000 (perl 1e+20); `9007199254740992/2` answers the exact integer (perl 4.5035996273705e+15); inexact division past 2**53 rounds ONCE from the exact rational (perl converts both operands to NV first and loses 2**53+1) -- guard row `div-o53` in Pl/t/perf-levers-04.t asserts PCL's answer; belongs in #1513's not-supported entry (s473a member 0), no local fix
